Subur Uddin vs The State Of Assam on 19 October, 2023

19.10.2023 Heard Shri SK Singha, learned counsel for the applicant, namely, Subur Uddin, who has filed this anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of the Cr.PC praying for pre-arrest bail in connection with Lanka PS Case No. 392/2023 under Sections 376(3)/511/506 of the IPC, read with Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012 and read with Section 67 of IT Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Also heard Shri B Sarma, learned Addl. Public Prosecutor, Assam, who has produced the Case Diary.
Shri KP Pathak, learned Amicus Curiae is also present for the respondent no. 2.

The projection made is that the petitioner was having love affair with the alleged victim and the version in the FIR is an exaggerated one.
The Addl. PP, however, submits that there are materials in the Case Diary which would implicate the petitioner.
This Court has examined the materials, including the statement of the alleged victim made under Section 164 of the Cr.PC.
In the said statement, definite allegations have been made against the petitioner which are consistent with the version of the informant, who is the mother of the alleged victim.

Shri Pathak, learned Amicus Curiae while endorsing the submission of Shri Sarma, learned Addl.
PP, further submits that the present may not be a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail as the presence of the applicant would be required for a proper and fair investigation.

Page No.# 3/3 In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, particularly taking into account the materials in the Case Diary, including the statement of the alleged victim made under Section 164 of the Cr.PC, the instant anticipatory bail application is rejected.

The Case Diary is returned back to the learned Addl. PP.
JUDGE
